measurements.formula: NDVI = (NIR reflectance - red reflectance) / (NIR reflectance + red reflectance)
measurements.mask_policy: Keep SCL 4 (vegetation) and 5 (not vegetated) on both dates; require valid red/NIR/SCL masks, nonzero raw DNs, nonnegative calibrated reflectance, and a finite positive denominator.
measurements.scope_note: Common valid land in the fixed landscape crop, including nonvegetated surfaces; this is not a parcel or crop-type mask.

change.formula: NDVI change = after NDVI - before NDVI
change.classification_rule: Decreased < -threshold; stable includes both boundaries; increased > threshold. Comparisons use the saved float32 differences and a float32 threshold.
change.scope_note: Demonstration tolerance, not a validated crop-change threshold. Shared valid land includes nonvegetated surfaces. Stable means within the tolerance, not proof of unchanged land or crops. SCL is automated at native 20 m resolution; two dates do not identify crop types or causes.

cases.question: Explain the saved mean NDVI for both dates, then give the increased, decreased and stable areas in hectares and percentages. State the valid pixel denominator, excluded pixels, and the change threshold.
cases.output:
### Observations

The application measurements for the two Sentinel-2B previews near Sidi Bennour show a saved mean NDVI of 0.4668 for 2024-02-20 and 0.4210 for 2025-02-14. The saved median NDVI is 0.4031 on the first date and 0.2924 on the second. The saved minimum and maximum values are -0.1436 and 0.9453 for the first date, and -0.0465 and 0.9421 for the second date. The saved pixelwise comparison on the common valid land sample uses 262,140 common valid pixels (2621.40 ha of valid area) as the percentage denominator, with 4 excluded pixels (0.04 ha of excluded area) and a demonstration change threshold of 0.05 NDVI units. The saved change classes are: Decreased NDVI: 895.25 ha (34.15%); Stable NDVI: 1274.86 ha (48.63%); Increased NDVI: 451.29 ha (17.22%). Decreased NDVI indicates pixels where the after NDVI was lower than the before NDVI by more than 0.05, increased NDVI indicates pixels where it was higher by more than 0.05, and stable NDVI indicates pixels within the plus or minus 0.05 tolerance.

### Evidence and interpretations

Normalized Difference Vegetation Index calculations use the near-infrared B08 and red B04 reflectance bands with the formula NDVI = (B08 - B04) / (B08 + B04), yielding values from -1 to 1 [MA_SENTINEL_NDVI_METHOD](https://custom-scripts.sentinel-hub.com/custom-scripts/sentinel-2/ndvi/). The index serves as a general proxy for live green vegetation [MA_SENTINEL_NDVI_METHOD](https://custom-scripts.sentinel-hub.com/custom-scripts/sentinel-2/ndvi/), where negative values relate to water, values near zero to barren surfaces, and positive values to vegetation [MA_SENTINEL_NDVI_METHOD](https://custom-scripts.sentinel-hub.com/custom-scripts/sentinel-2/ndvi/). These general interpretations do not provide field-specific diagnoses [MA_SENTINEL_NDVI_METHOD](https://custom-scripts.sentinel-hub.com/custom-scripts/sentinel-2/ndvi/). The saved measurements and change classes describe the same valid land pixels on both dates, including nonvegetated surfaces, but do not establish parcel boundaries, crop identity, continuous trends, or the causes of change such as weather, irrigation, harvest, or rotation.

### Next checks

Review local agricultural calendars, crop rotation records, and irrigation schedules to understand seasonal management differences between the two dates. Inspect official parcel boundary maps and consult local farm advisors or field inspections to verify crop types, soil conditions, and actual plant health. Examine additional cloud-free satellite dates across the growing season to establish whether the observed index differences reflect temporary crop cycles or longer-term changes.

cases.question: Explique les moyennes NDVI pour les deux dates et donne les surfaces en hectares et pourcentages en hausse, en baisse et stables. Précise les limites de cette classification.
cases.output:
### Observations

Les moyennes NDVI enregistrées pour la zone d'étude sont de 0,4668 pour la date du 20 février 2024 et de 0,4210 pour la date du 14 février 2025. La médiane passe quant à elle de 0,4031 à 0,2924 entre ces deux périodes. L'analyse comparative pixel par pixel de l'échantillon valide commun, couvrant une superficie totale valide de 2621,40 ha (avec 0,04 ha exclus), répartit les évolutions selon les classes suivantes : NDVI en baisse : 895,25 ha (34,15%) ; NDVI stable : 1274,86 ha (48,63%) ; NDVI en hausse : 451,29 ha (17,21%). Ces statistiques décrivent l'ensemble de la surface valide incluant les zones non végétalisées.

### Références et interprétations

L'indice de végétation par différence normalisée (NDVI) se calcule à partir des bandes infrarouge proche B08 et rouge B04 selon la formule NDVI = (B08 - B04) / (B08 + B04), l'indice variant de -1 à 1 en tant que proxy de la végétation verte vivante [MA_SENTINEL_NDVI_METHOD](https://custom-scripts.sentinel-hub.com/custom-scripts/sentinel-2/ndvi/). Les valeurs négatives s'associent généralement à l'eau, les valeurs proches de zéro aux surfaces dénuées de végétation, et les valeurs positives à la végétation [MA_SENTINEL_NDVI_METHOD](https://custom-scripts.sentinel-hub.com/custom-scripts/sentinel-2/ndvi/). Ces interprétations demeurent générales et ne constituent pas un diagnostic spécifique au terrain [MA_SENTINEL_NDVI_METHOD](https://custom-scripts.sentinel-hub.com/custom-scripts/sentinel-2/ndvi/). Par ailleurs, les variations observées et les seuils de tolérance appliqués ne permettent pas à eux seuls d'identifier des types de cultures précis, des pertes de rendement ou les causes exactes des changements constatés.

### Vérifications à réaliser

Il est recommandé d'effectuer des vérifications complémentaires pour interpréter ces résultats, notamment en intégrant des observations de terrain sur les pratiques agricoles locales, les rotations de cultures et les calendriers de semis ou de récolte. L'examen de données météorologiques détaillées, telles que les relevés de précipitations et d'irrigation, ainsi que l'utilisation de séries temporelles plus denses et de contours de parcelles validés, permettra de mieux contextualiser ces variations interannuelles.
